turns.question: Among the 1,000 most liquid US stocks, which three had the strongest and which three the weakest returns from January 2, 2025 through March 12, 2026?

report.markdown:
**Strongest returns (top 3):**

| Rank | Ticker | Return | Z-score | Observations |
|------|--------|--------|---------|--------------|
| 1 | DFDV | **+36.53%** | 22.51 | 297 / 298 |
| 2 | AXTI | **+20.34%** | 12.46 | 298 / 298 |
| 3 | ABVX | **+15.05%** | 9.18 | 298 / 298 |

**Weakest returns (bottom 3):**

| Rank | Ticker | Return | Z-score | Observations |
|------|--------|--------|---------|--------------|
| 1 | DOGZ | **−96.50%** | −0.75 | 298 / 298 |
| 2 | CHOW | **−96.07%** | −0.75 | 123 / 298 (41% coverage) |
| 3 | DFNS | **−95.77%** | −0.74 | 298 / 298 |

The window covers the full dataset period (January 2, 2025 – March 12, 2026) across the 1,000 most liquid U.S. stocks. Returns are measured from the close before the first session to the last close. The bottom three all lost over 95% of value; CHOW has notably lower data coverage (41%). [1][2]
